headline: CoreWeave's outlook revives the AI trade; chips jump 5.7%, S&P 500 +1.3%, Nasdaq +1.6%
summary: Stocks opened higher on CoreWeave's results, dipped briefly early (S&P 500 low 7,571.88), then climbed to 7,647.20 by the afternoon before easing slightly into the close. Tech was the best of the 11 S&P sectors at +2.7% and all 30 SOX members rose, while the equal-weight S&P gained only about 0.8% and Microsoft, Meta and Amazon slipped; advancers led decliners about 1.5 to 1 on the NYSE on light volume. With the Treasury market shut for Veterans Day, the VIX fell for a fourth day to a one-week low.
drivers: CoreWeave jumped 24.7% to $60.77, its best day in over three months, after a revenue beat, a 2026 revenue forecast raised to $13.0–13.3 billion, about $9 billion of expected customer prepayments, no plans for costlier debt through 2027 and a target of adjusted profitability in early 2028. Fellow AI-capacity names followed: Nebius +15.4%, Dell +11.8%, Oracle +8.8%, Bloom Energy +13.0%.

The SOX rose 5.66% to 10,564.11, its highest close since Nov 3, with every member up: Arm +12.1%, Micron +11.9%, Marvell +9.3%, Intel +7.5%, AMD +7.3%, Lam and Applied Materials about +6%, Broadcom +4.0% and Sandisk +13.7%. Chip stocks alone added roughly 0.8 point of the S&P 500's 1.3% gain.
Nvidia steadies after its CEO-probe slide

Nvidia rose 2.9% to $173.73, its first gain after losing nearly 10% (about $430 billion of market value) in two sessions over the board probe into Jensen Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese spy; it remains about 27% below its October record.
Hike bets and Anthropic weigh on parts of Big Tech

Futures still fully price a December Fed hike after Tuesday's hot CPI, with about 10% odds of a half point, and the dollar index rose about 0.7% with cash Treasuries closed. Microsoft fell about 2.3% for a second day after Anthropic launched Office-style Claude tools ahead of its IPO (range $70–78, up to about $1.4 trillion), and Meta and Amazon each lost about 2%. WTI rose 0.6% to $86.53 off two-month lows as Iran hardened its stance on nuclear material.
week: Week to date the S&P 500 is up 3.3%, the Nasdaq 3.6%, the Russell 2000 3.3% and the Dow 2.3%, leaving the S&P 500 about 2.6% below its October record after last week's AI-led selloff, though a December Fed hike is fully priced and the 10-year yield sits near 5%.
watch: Next: Treasuries reopen Thursday, Nebius reports before the open, jobless claims are out, and Cisco and Applied Materials report after the close; October PPI follows Friday, with Anthropic's IPO set to price Nov 18 and the Fed meeting Dec 8–9.
